cls.quote: The Performance Line CX system includes a handlebar-mounted Bosch MiniRemote to shift through the various levels of pedal assist. It also includes the top tube integrated Bosch System Controller display to monitor battery levels and pedal assist mode. Curiously, we couldn’t find the Muga’s e-bike classification or top speed listed anywhere on the brand’s website or in the press materials, but it’s fair to assume that it will comply with regional regulations and standards. ⟶ A look inside the Muga frame.

spd.quote: Muga 10 20mph ⟶ A 29″ aluminum frame full suspension trail e-bike with high-end components.

tq.quote: Worth mentioning, is that with the new update from Bosch, this CX drive unit will be a candidate for 750W of peak power and 100Nm of torque. Having spent some time on various eMTB’s with the new update, it is quite the dramatic increase in power that impressively doesn’t take away too much of the range.
tq.basis: Muga launch story; 100Nm only after a Bosch software update; no stock torque given

wh.quote: Between the three complete Muga builds currently offered, riders have the option to choose either a longer-range 750 Wh battery (Muga 10 and 20) or a lighter-weight 600 Wh battery (Muga 30). Along with those options, riders can add the optional Bosch PowerMore 250 Wh Range Extender ($549) when purchasing to bump the battery capacity up to 1,000 Wh or 850 Wh, respectively. ⟶ Integrated Safety Features
